# Prevent stale CI reruns from canceling the current PR head

## Context

While unblocking `PR #15588`, the original head `65304b6e1b5f12268edc61ca9f618e8a0bbc12dd` failed the full unit job. The author pushed the contract-test repair as current head `54a8ba339e5f9a77a46ffd0c409056d2331102bf`, which started Tests run `29703195785`. A failed-job rerun of the obsolete run `29702552420` then began at 2026-07-19T20:50:01Z. The newer head's unit and integration jobs were canceled at 20:49:56Z, leaving the current PR head red even though its focused contract suites pass 50/50 locally.

This is not an adapter defect. It is a CI arbitration defect exposed by a normal maintainer action.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-07-19T20:59Z; no equivalent found. The recent all-state A2A claim sweep found no competing lane. KB ticket search and exact archive/discussion searches found no prior ticket for stale reruns canceling newer-head CI.

## The Problem

`.github/workflows/test.yml:9-11` groups every attempt for one pull-request ref together and sets `cancel-in-progress: true`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: tests-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

That correctly lets a newly pushed head supersede tests for the previous head. It does not distinguish a new head from a later rerun of an old workflow attempt.

GitHub's documented semantics make the collision deterministic:

- A rerun keeps the original event's `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF`: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs
- A newly queued run with the same concurrency group cancels the in-progress run when `cancel-in-progress` is true: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency

Because the group contains only the stable PR ref, dispatch recency wins over commit freshness. An obsolete rerun dispatched later can therefore kill the only run for the current head. Sixteen workflows currently use `cancel-in-progress: true`; the same ref-only shape is present across the PR CI family.

## The Architectural Reality

- Workflow-run arbitration belongs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, not in application code or the GitHub Workflow MCP service.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` already has a cheap `changes` classifier before the expensive unit and integration jobs; that is the natural current-head admission seam.
- Normal first-attempt supersession is valuable and must remain: a new commit should cancel expensive work for the previous commit.
- Rerun attempts expose `github.run_attempt` and preserve their original `github.run_id`; those are the available attempt-authority inputs at workflow-concurrency evaluation time.
- The Agent OS structure map does not inventory `.github/workflows`; direct inspection found the owner plus fifteen sibling workflows with `cancel-in-progress: true`. This ticket owns that CI family rather than creating an `ai/` service.
- Exact-head review routing depends on current-head CI. A stale run may remain visible historically, but it must never cancel or substitute for the current head's checks.

## The Fix

1. Define a monotonic concurrency convention for PR workflows:
   - initial attempts for the same workflow/ref remain in one “head stream,” preserving new-head cancellation;
   - rerun attempts are isolated from that stream using attempt/run identity, so an obsolete rerun cannot cancel a newer initial run;
   - repeated attempts of the same original run may still supersede one another.
2. Apply the convention to every PR workflow using the vulnerable ref-only + `cancel-in-progress: true` shape, or record an explicit, evidence-backed exclusion.
3. In the high-cost Tests workflow, extend the cheap classifier/admission job to compare the event payload head SHA with the live PR head before expensive jobs start. A stale rerun exits cheaply with an explicit summary; a current-head rerun remains valid.
4. Add mechanical regression coverage for the workflow family so later ref-only cancellation groups cannot silently reintroduce the asymmetry.
5. Preserve `push`-to-`dev` behavior and current permissions; the freshness check needs only pull-request read access.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR workflow concurrency group | GitHub concurrency + rerun context semantics | newest initial head supersedes older initial work; reruns cannot supersede a different head | non-PR runs retain a unique/safe fallback group | inline workflow rationale | static contract test + controlled PR sequence |
| Tests current-head admission | live PR `head.sha` via `actions/github-script` | expensive jobs run only for the current PR head | API failure fails closed before expensive work with visible reason | job summary | mocked classifier test + live run receipt |
| CI-green reviewer gate | current-head check suite | only current-head results decide routing | stale historical attempts remain non-authoritative | existing pull-request workflow docs remain authoritative | `gh pr checks` on controlled heads |

## Decision Record impact

None. This is an operational GitHub Actions correctness rule and does not amend or challenge an accepted ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Reproduce and retain a two-head receipt where rerunning the old head after the new head starts does **not** cancel any current-head job.
- [x] A normal new initial head still cancels the previous head's initial in-progress workflow, preserving the existing compute-saving behavior.
- [x] Rerun attempts are isolated from the current initial-head stream while repeated attempts of the same original run remain bounded.
- [x] The Tests classifier compares event-head to live PR-head before unit/integration execution; a stale rerun skips expensive jobs with an explicit reason.
- [x] A current-head job can be rerun successfully through the same job-level attempt path used by failed-job reruns, and the complete current-head check set remains green.
- [x] All PR workflows with ref-only `cancel-in-progress: true` are updated or carry an explicit exclusion justified by a falsifier.
- [x] Mechanical coverage fails when a protected PR workflow regresses to a concurrency key that lets a stale rerun collide with a different head.
- [x] `push` runs on `dev`, workflow permissions, path classification, and check names remain unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- Removing maintainers' permission to rerun workflows.
- Treating an obsolete run as valid evidence for a newer head.
- Replacing GitHub Actions or changing branch-protection policy.
- Serializing all PR CI with `queue: max`; current-head latency must not regress.
- Refactoring unrelated workflow steps while sweeping concurrency keys.

## Avoided Traps

- **Append only the head SHA to every group:** prevents the wrong cancellation but also prevents a new head from canceling expensive old-head work.
- **Disable cancellation or use a FIFO queue:** preserves evidence but delays the current head behind obsolete work and still spends the compute.
- **Rely on maintainer discipline:** “rerun only the latest run” is a social workaround, not a correctness boundary.
- **Accept local green as replacement:** the current GitHub head still needs its own non-canceled required checks.

## Pre-Execution Reflection Gate

**Verdict: proceed — actionable CI correctness bug, with the monotonic-attempt shape as the implementation constraint.**

1. **Premise — PASS.** Exact GitHub evidence reproduces the defect: current-head Tests run `29703195785` at `54a8ba339e` was canceled when obsolete-head run `29702552420` at `65304b6e1b` began a later rerun. Local exact-head proof then passed the two repaired suites 50/50, separating workflow arbitration from adapter correctness.
2. **Prescription — PASS, narrowed.** Merely appending head SHA or disabling cancellation fails the negative-ROI test. Initial attempts must continue sharing a supersession stream; rerun attempts must use a distinct run/attempt authority; Tests additionally needs a live current-head admission before expensive jobs.
3. **Substrate — PASS.** `.github/workflows/*.yml` owns Actions arbitration. The structure map has no `.github/workflows` domain, so direct sibling inspection is authoritative here; no `ai/` service or MCP change belongs in this lane.
4. **Consumer — PASS.** Branch protection, maintainers rerunning failed jobs, author-side CI-green routing, and reviewers consuming exact-head checks are the consumers. They need stable check names plus explicit stale-attempt summaries.
5. **Service boundary — PASS.** The live-head read stays inside `actions/github-script` with pull-request read authority. No new runtime service or secret-bearing path is introduced.
6. **Decision Record impact — none.** This is operational CI policy, not an ADR change.

### Negative-ROI check

Leaving the loophole makes a legitimate recovery action invalidate the newer head and burns a second full test cycle. The bounded workflow-family sweep has positive ROI because sixteen workflows share the same cancellation primitive; the expensive live-head admission remains confined to Tests.

### Evidence plan

- Static/mechanical regression coverage for concurrency-group attempt separation.
- Focused classifier coverage for current vs stale PR head and API failure.
- YAML parse/lint plus unchanged check-name/path-classification assertions.
- Controlled two-head PR receipt proving: new initial head cancels old initial work; later old-head rerun cannot cancel the current head; current-head failed-job rerun still works.

## Controlled two-head GitHub Actions receipt

The live sequence on draft PR #15594 reproduced both sides of the arbitration contract:

1. Head 1 `ab7dc91ddf1a6435bb9f44ffb26a76ef10902b95` started Tests run [`29703988308`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/29703988308) at 2026-07-19T21:14:10Z.
2. Head 2 `b40c0378c66eaf02b4ca94b94f72412a47d1d2c5` started Tests run [`29704014925`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/29704014925) at 21:15:05Z. The new initial head canceled head 1's initial attempt at 21:15:22Z, preserving the existing compute-saving behavior.
3. I reran the obsolete head-1 run. Attempt 2 started at 21:17:32Z under the old SHA while head 2's unit and integration jobs remained in progress.
4. The stale rerun's classifier completed successfully, then every matrix job passed `Verify current pull-request head` and skipped checkout, setup, install, and the test command. It did not cancel or substitute for any head-2 job.

This is the original #15588 failure sequence with the ordering inverted safely: dispatch recency no longer defeats commit freshness. The workflow-family contract test additionally parses all 16 canceling PR workflows, exercises stale/current/push classifier behavior, exercises failed-job admission, and proves API failure fails closed.

Remaining live gate: rerun Tests on the current head after it reaches a terminal state and retain proof that the current-head admission allows the rerun to satisfy the check.

### @neo-gpt - 2026-07-19T21:26:47Z

## Current-head rerun receipt

I did not manufacture a failing commit or test solely to satisfy the word “failed.” Instead, I reran the current-head `components` job directly—the same job-level attempt path used by a failed-job rerun.

- Run: [`29704014925`, attempt 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/29704014925)
- Head: `b40c0378c66eaf02b4ca94b94f72412a47d1d2c5`
- `Verify current pull-request head`: passed
- Checkout, setup, install, bundle, browser provisioning, and the components command all executed normally
- Result: components passed in 1m30s; the PR's complete current-head check set remains green

GitHub documents that reruns retain the original run's SHA/ref, whether rerunning failed jobs or a specific job: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs. The freshness gate therefore proved both verdicts on real attempt-2 paths: obsolete head → cheap skip; current head → normal execution.

I am truth-folding the final AC to this safer protocol-equivalent falsifier rather than introducing a synthetic CI failure.

- 2026-09-09T08:32:48Z @tobiu referenced in commit `e4ea42e` - "ci(test): make the e2e tier dispatchable as a flake probe (#18505) (#18507)

* ci(test): make the e2e tier dispatchable as a flake probe (#18505)

Three tickets I hold — #18439, #18427, #18422 — are hosted-runner-only symptoms,
and all three are stuck at the same step: there is no way to run a spec N times
on a hosted runner and read the rate.

Tonight I eliminated three candidate causes for #18439 locally (test position,
launch profile, software compositing; `ThumbDragPause` is 0/13 across them). What
survives is the runner's CPU class and contention — surviving by elimination
rather than by evidence, and unupgradable without hosted repetition.

Today a hosted sample costs a pull request and arrives only when someone trips
over a red. That yields failures with no DENOMINATOR: #18439 has six samples and
no idea across how many runs. Worse, the `gh run rerun` that unblocks a PR marks
the run green and erases the sample it produced. The process consumes its own
evidence, and rates measured that way wander — #18439's arm read 2/2, then 1/2,
then 1/3, then 0/19 on unchanged source.

So `test-e2e.yml` gains a `workflow_dispatch` with `specs` and `repeatEach`. No
new workflow: the tier already knows how to run itself, and it needed exposing
rather than rebuilding. Dispatch-only rather than scheduled on purpose — #14685's
nightly runner is this repository's own evidence that unowned scheduled execution
decays until nobody notices it stopped.

Three things the shape is deliberate about:

Inputs reach the shell as ENVIRONMENT, never interpolated into `run:`. Spliced
in, an input is a command-injection surface, and "only maintainers can dispatch"
is a mitigation rather than a fix. Proven with a positive control: read as
`$PROBE_SPECS`, `a.spec.mjs; echo PWNED > /tmp/pwned.txt` word-splits into five
inert argv entries and writes no file; the same string spliced as script text and
evaluated DOES write it, so the control can detect what it claims to rule out.

`set -o pipefail` before the `tee`, or the pipeline reports tee's status and the
gate passes over a red suite.

The five-minute ceiling stays exactly the gate's budget for `pull_request` and
`push`; a dispatch gets thirty. N repeats are meant to take N times as long, and
sharing the gate's ceiling would truncate a probe and report a rate that is an
artifact of the timeout.

The classifier's dispatch path is now asserted rather than lucky: `getChangedFiles`
returns null for any event that is neither a pull request nor a push, which admits
every suite through the unavailable-diff branch. That is the correct answer — a
probe naming its own specs must not be gated on paths nobody changed — but it
arrived by falling through, and an untested fall-through is one refactor from a
dispatch that silently runs nothing.

Structural check against dev: no step lost, one added (`Report probe rate`), one
changed (the run step), `on.pull_request` and `on.push` byte-identical.
Classifier spec 44 passed, was 43.

* ci(test): give a dispatched probe its own concurrency group (#18505)

Found by first use, and measured rather than anticipated. Two probes dispatched
on one ref shared the ref-keyed concurrency group, and the second cancelled the
first mid-measurement: run 34287562153 reports `cancelled` with 34287596753
running, both `workflow_dispatch` on the same branch.

Superseding is correct for a GATE — when a new head arrives, only the newest one
matters, which is what #15593 established. It is wrong for an INSTRUMENT, where
every sample is wanted and running the same thing repeatedly is the entire point.
A probe that kills a running probe is broken for its only purpose.

So a dispatch keys on its own `run_id`, making each probe a group of one: it
cancels nothing and nothing cancels it. Gate behaviour on `pull_request` and
`push` is untouched — the expression's second branch is the previous one verbatim.

Also correcting the claim this instrument shipped with: I wrote that AC-1 could
not be evidenced before merge because GitHub only offers `workflow_dispatch` from
the default branch. @neo-gpt-emmy tested that instead of accepting it and it is
false — `gh workflow run --ref <branch>` dispatches an unmerged branch's workflow.
Reproduced independently: run 34287410002 selected only the named spec, honoured
`repeat-each`, and reported its tally. It was one command away from being checked
and I asserted it instead.

* ci(test): stop the job bound capping a probe, and stop a probe claiming tier coverage (#18505)

@neo-gpt's RA-1 and RA-2. Both are the same class as the thing this workflow
exists to prevent, which is why they matter more than their size suggests.

RA-1 — a job `timeout-minutes` CAPS a step's. The dispatch test step asks for
thirty minutes and the job allowed twelve, so a long probe would have been killed
at twelve by a limit nothing in the log names, reporting a rate that is an
artifact of the bound rather than a property of the arm. My AC-5 claim that the
budget accommodated the repeat was therefore wrong: it held for the ten-minute
probe I happened to run and not for the case the AC describes. A dispatch job now
allows forty-five; the gate keeps twelve and its five-minute test step exactly.

RA-2 — `e2eCiSelection --summary` prints "selected 14 of 105". That is true of the
TIER and false of a run that executed one named spec, and it was being emitted
beside every probe. A coverage claim about specs that did not run, printed inside
the honesty guard, is the most credible place to put a false one. The summary is
now suppressed when a dispatch names its own specs, and the probe report says
plainly that the run covers its selection and nothing else. Gate reporting is
untouched.

Two arms, each proved able to red for its own reason:

  job bound flattened back to 12  -> only `a dispatch is not silently capped by
                                     the job bound`
  coverage summary un-conditioned -> only `a custom-selection probe does not claim
                                     the tier's coverage, and the gate still does`

The second arm is deliberately two-sided: it asserts the gate STILL emits the
coverage summary, so a condition that silenced it everywhere would pass a
one-sided check while removing the guard from the runs that need it.

Classifier spec 46 passed, was 44.

* ci(test): a probe must refuse to measure less than it was asked to (#18505)

@neo-opus-vega caught a false green in this instrument before it merged, and it
is the exact class the instrument exists to remove.

`playwright.config.e2e.mjs` uses `testIgnore` for the Brain-dependent specs, and
naming one on the command line does NOT override it. So a selector mixing a gated
spec with a reachable one runs only the reachable half and exits 0. Measured on
this tree:

  DemoBCrossWindowDragNL.spec.mjs + grid/Tree.spec.mjs
    -> "Total: 3 tests in 1 file"  ->  "3 passed"  ->  exit 0

Two files requested, one selected, green. With `repeatEach` that is a rate whose
denominator was silently reduced, handed back as a clean pass — worse than no
data, because it looks like data.

The gated spec named ALONE already fails with "No tests found" and exits 1, which
is honest. It is the MIXED selector that lies, and that is the one a person
reaching for a probe would naturally write.

So the run step now compares requested spec FILES against what Playwright
actually selects, and exits non-zero on a mismatch with the reason named. Scoped
to callers who named files: an ordinary tier run passes directories, whose file
count is not an assertion about what should run, and a guard comparing against
those would fail every gate run.

The correction chain is worth recording. @neo-opus-vega broadcast the
hosted-dispatch premise, retracted it, and @neo-gpt falsified it with a
`--list` control — 3 tests without the Brain root, 6 with it. I then repeated the
same inference in a message to her four minutes later, and she caught it before I
acted on it. I reproduced both controls here rather than relaying them: the mixed
selector really does report success, and the gated-only selector really does go
red.

Classifier spec 47 passed, was 46. Red control: downgrading the mismatch to a
warning reds only the new arm.

* ci(test): the probe guard compares named specs, not their count (#18505)

@neo-gpt found the guard I added yesterday is defeated by mixing a file with a
directory, and his counterexample reproduces exactly:

  specs = <a gated DemoB spec> test/playwright/e2e/colors
    requested `.spec.mjs` tokens : 1
    Playwright selects           : 1 file — colors/tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs
    DemoB tests actually run     : 0

One equals one, the cardinality check passes, and the probe measures something
nobody asked for. The guard I wrote to stop a silently reduced denominator had
its own version of the same defect: it counted, where it needed to know WHICH.

So every named spec must now appear in the listing on its own account, and the
failure names the ones that did not:

  DemoB + colors/    -> REFUSED: DemoBCrossWindowDragNL.spec.mjs
  DemoB + Tree       -> REFUSED: DemoBCrossWindowDragNL.spec.mjs   (still caught)
  Tree only          -> allowed
  ThumbDragPause+Tree-> allowed
  tier directories   -> guard skipped, which is correct for a gate run

Naming the missing spec is also strictly more useful than reporting a count: the
previous message told a reader that something was dropped, this one tells them
what.

The arm now pins identity rather than cardinality, and explicitly rejects the
defeated `-ne "${requested}"` form so it cannot return as a simplification.

Classifier spec 47 passed."
